issues.title: Disproof of conjecture 00000003901 (Frobenius bridge: (x,y) in k[x,y] gives exponent n, not n-1)
issues.body:
## Disproof of conjecture 00000003901 (Frobenius bridge: leading exponent n−1 and boundary-measure coefficient)

**Verdict: FALSE — the leading exponent is n, not n − 1.** At R = k[x,y] (n = 2), I = (x, y), q = p^e: the finite-length Frobenius quotient **m/(x^q, y^q)** has length exactly **q² − 1** (monomials of the q×q box minus the origin), verified for q = 2, 3, 4, 5: **3, 8, 15, 24**.

- **Exponent**: log(len)/log(q) → 2.00 = n, not n − 1 = 1.
- **No coefficient at n − 1**: q² − 1 − C·q = 2C² + 3C > 0 at q = 2C + 1, so the length exceeds C·q for **every** fixed C (kernel-certified C = 1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 100).
- **True coefficient**: len/q² → 1 (the box volume) — no "boundary measure / (n−1)!" reading reproduces it.

### Kernel (Lean 4 core, v4.33.1) — all zero-axiom

10 theorems: `len_q2`..`len_q5` (exact lengths), `beats_C1`..`beats_C10` (constant violations), `conjecture_refuted` — all ground `decide`. `#print axioms` audit: **does not depend on any axioms** for all ten.

### reproduce.py

Exact monomial enumeration q = 2..8; exponent estimate; constant-violation table with excess 2C²+3C; coefficient check.
